The two repository-side conditions are closed and are now enforced by a check that has been observed to fail.

checks.name: Protected write boundary
checks.command: gh api repos/bext-stack/automonique/branches/main/protection; gh api repos/bext-stack/automonique/rulesets; gh api repos/bext-stack/automonique --jq .permissions
checks.output: Measured read-only against the configured remote on 2026-08-11. Branch protection: HTTP 404 'Branch not protected'. Rulesets: []. Repository visibility: public. The ambient developer credential present in this environment reports permissions {admin:true, maintain:true, push:true, triage:true, pull:true}. A non-integration credential therefore CAN write to main, which is the opposite of what this row requires. No push was attempted: plan/authority.toml denies push and administer_repository, and the absence of protection is conclusive without one. Proving the affirmative later still requires the rejected-push transcript named in the contract's Completion evidence; configuration alone is a forbidden shortcut for this row.

checks.name: Signature verifies
checks.command: git verify-commit HEAD; git log --format=%G? HEAD | sort | uniq -c; gh api 'repos/bext-stack/automonique/commits?per_page=100' --jq '[.[] | .commit.verification.verified] | group_by(.) | map({v:.[0], n:length})'
checks.reason: Signing is not enabled, so the row's antecedent does not hold and there is no signature to verify. Enabling it requires generating key material and publishing a trust root, which is external administration under GOVERNANCE.md and outside worker authority.
checks.output: What was observed instead: `git verify-commit HEAD` exits 1 with empty stdout and empty stderr; all 78 commits reachable from HEAD report signature status N (unsigned); the remote reports [{v:false, n:79}] with reason 'unsigned' for its main tip. The enforcement half WAS measured: setting signing = "ssh" in the checked-in register produced 'REGISTER declares a signing identity but no signing_effective_commit', and with an effective commit set the fixture produced '`git verify-commit` does not accept it' per commit (.github/identity/test_check_identity.py::test_declared_signing_over_unsigned_commits). The reverse direction — a signed commit under signing = "none" — is exercised at the function boundary with a synthesised commit record, because producing a genuinely signed commit needs a key this environment does not have; that limitation is stated in the test's docstring.

checks.name: Declared separation
checks.output: Exit 0: 'ok — evidence_files 37, identities 1, exceptions 3, commits 78, excused 3, wrong_identity 0, wrong_trailer 0, signature_required 0, signature_verified 0'. This passes vacuously and says so: .github/identity/register.toml declares separation_claimed = false and one shared identity holding all five GOVERNANCE.md roles, so NO identity is claimed as separate and no separation exists. What is measured is that the claim cannot be made falsely. Breaking it on the real tree: separation_claimed = true produced 'separation_claimed is true, but these identities are not dedicated: candidate — identity separation is not achieved' (exit 1); restoring produced exit 0 with a byte-identical file. Two dedicated identities sharing one fingerprint produce 'share one fingerprint; they are one credential', and a dedicated identity with signing = "none" produces 'declared dedicated but signs nothing' (fixture tests). Deleting one historical_exception from the checked-in register produced 'commit 69db4ca8 is authored by an identity .github/identity/register.toml does not list' plus the committer line (exit 1); repointing an exception at HEAD produced 'historical_exception 606ff48c is not an ancestor of rule_effective_commit 868a97d3, so the rule was already in force when it was made' (exit 1). Each break was restored and re-run to exit 0.

On the register side the shared identity is recorded as separation = "shared", not as five separate roles. This record itself claims zero reviewers and zero independent review.

notes: GATE-IDENTITY IS NOT CLOSED and BOOT-002 is not complete. Two of its four closing conditions are external administrative facts that do not exist, and the contract forbids closing this gate on configuration that has never refused a push. What landed is the repository-side half: a register of record with a closed vocabulary (.github/identity/register.toml), a standalone checker (.github/identity/check_identity.py) with its own main() returning an exit code, 38 unit tests, and a CI workflow. Wiring the checker into plan/check.py is deliberately left to the integrator, per the instruction not to edit plan/check.py from a parallel worker. Three findings that are facts about this repository rather than achievements of this item: (1) main on the configured remote has no branch protection and no ruleset, the repository is public, and the ambient developer credential holds admin and push, so any credential that can reach the remote can write main today; (2) commit 69db4ca8 was authored and committed under a personal name and email address, which AGENTS.md forbids — the 2026-08-10 rewrite covered three other commits and did not reach this one, and rewriting history is out of scope for this contract, so it is pinned as a historical exception rather than silently allowed; (3) tools/scrub/scan.py scans commit messages and blob contents but not commit author or committer fields, so the personal address in (2) is invisible to it — that is an observation for the owner, not a change made here, since tools/scrub/ is outside this item's lease. On evidence vocabulary: the orchestration brief asked for a result of "unmeasured", but plan/doctrine.md § Evidence and plan/gate.py define an unmeasured check as "result": null with a "reason", and gate.py refuses any other string. The two unmeasurable rows use null with a reason and record what WAS observed under "output" as well. No independent review of any kind occurred: one agent wrote the register, the checker, the tests and this file, and read its own diff. That is a self-review and is not independent.
